codeReview.summary: The fix removes the default-user fallback and closes the original unauthenticated-handshake acceptance bug, but it introduces a blocking integration regression: the frontend still sends X-User-Id only in STOMP connectHeaders, while the backend now requires that value during the SockJS/HTTP handshake.

issues.description: Handshake now hard-rejects missing X-User-Id (lines 36-37), but the frontend provides X-User-Id only in STOMP connectHeaders (frontend/src/hooks/useWebSocket.ts:68-70). Per architecture note, connectHeaders do not affect handshake auth, so browser SockJS clients are rejected before CONNECT and WebSocket alerts regress.

Feature description requested an integration test proving unauthenticated WebSocket connection rejection, but the fix adds only unit tests for beforeHandshake (commit touches only WebSocketAuthInterceptor.java and WebSocketAuthInterceptorTest.java).

sharedStateObservations.observation: Auth guidance for fake-auth WebSocket flows is split and incomplete in AGENTS.md: it mentions fake auth and /ws STOMP endpoint but not the handshake-vs-connectHeaders constraint, which can lead to backend-only auth fixes that break browser connectivity.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: AGENTS.md:61,63; architecture.md:16 explicitly says handshake identity is from SockJS/HTTP and connectHeaders do not affect it; frontend/src/hooks/useWebSocket.ts:68-70 uses connectHeaders only.

summary: Original blocking fallback issue is removed, but the fix is not acceptable yet because strict handshake header enforcement is incompatible with the current frontend connection path, causing a new blocking regression in WebSocket connectivity.
